chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the sun sets, the time for the two prayers enters, except that this one is before this one.

key_terms.الصَّلَاتَيْنِ: The two prayers (referring to Maghrib and 'Isha)
key_terms.غَرَبَتِ الشَّمْسُ: The sun sets (specifically referring to the disappearance of the sun's disk below the horizon)
key_terms.هَذِهِ قَبْلَ هَذِهِ: This one before this one (indicating the chronological order of the two prayer times)

ai.seo_question: When does the time for Maghrib and Isha prayers begin according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the entry time for Maghrib and 'Isha prayers based on the sun's setting (ghurub), a foundational principle in Shia fiqh. It clarifies that while both prayers are linked to this single celestial event, Maghrib time immediately precedes 'Isha, emphasizing the distinct temporal boundaries for each obligation. This narration underscores the precision required in determining prayer times according to the Imams' teachings.
